expectedObservations.statement: The condenser fan motor was seized and replaced with a 1/4 HP 1075 RPM motor and new 5 uF capacitor.
Fan amp draw was 1.1 A against a 1.4 A nameplate.
Homeowner reports the motor replacement on 2026-08-12.

expectedGaps.description: Warranty terms for the replaced motor are not documented.

caseSummary: Homeowner believes the heat pump is under warranty; data plate suggests an older unit.

artifacts.text: Our heat pump was installed new in 2019, so it should still be under warranty, right? - [NAME]
Heat pump outdoor unit data plate: manufacture date code indicates 2014. Serial recorded in job photos. Coil fin corrosion on the lower 6 in.

expectedObservations.statement: Homeowner says the heat pump was installed new in 2019.
The data plate manufacture date code indicates 2014.
Coil fins are corroded on the lower 6 inches.

expectedConflicts.description: The homeowner-reported install year (2019) and the data-plate manufacture year (2014) differ; the install date is unverified.

expectedGaps.description: Installation records or warranty registration are needed.

expectedObservations.statement: Line 1 is a Standard Repair for $1,150.00 covering a high pressure limit switch, filter drier, 11 lbs of 422B refrigerant, and nitrogen leak test, evacuation, recharge and operation test.
Line 2 is a Standard Repair for $1,215.00 covering blower motor belts, drain lines, evaporator and condenser coil cleaning, and bacterial growth remediation where possible.
11 lbs of 422B refrigerant is listed.
Subtotal and job total are $2,365.00, equal to $1,150.00 + $1,215.00.
Payment terms are upon receipt.

expectedGaps.description: The invoice shows no warranty-validity dates, which the owners require on customer invoices.
No equipment make, model or serial is shown.
Component prices are not itemized within the flat-rate lines.
The meaning of the (2) markers (two systems, two units or quantity) is not stated.
The referenced Terms & Conditions are not included.

forbiddenClaims.description: Assigns prices to individual components inside the flat-rate lines.
States as fact that two systems or units were serviced.
Invents a diagnosis or failure cause not stated (e.g., where the leak was or why the switch failed).
States a warranty duration, start/end date or coverage scope that is not in the supplied material.
